definition: Consecrate means to dedicate something as sacred in a formal, solemn ceremony.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word consecrate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know consecrate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The village elders gathered at dawn to consecrate the new well to the memory of the flood's victims.
Dedicate is the everyday, weaker cousin — you can dedicate a book, a bench, or a season to almost anything; consecrate adds formal ceremony and a holy or solemn purpose.
Sanctify is stronger still: it claims the thing has actually been made holy, while consecrate emphasizes the formal act of setting it apart.

Bless means to call down divine favor or protection on someone or something, often with a short prayer or gesture. Consecrate goes further and is more formal: in a solemn ceremony, a person with authority sets a thing apart as sacred from then on. A meal can be blessed in a moment; a chapel is consecrated for good.

Enshrine means to preserve something as precious and untouchable - relics kept in a shrine, or rights enshrined in a constitution. Consecrate is the formal, solemn act that first declares a thing sacred. Enshrining protects what is already treasured; consecrating is the ceremony that sets it apart to begin with.

You consecrate ground, buildings, or even a life to a purpose; for casual commitments ('she dedicated her weekend to studying'), dedicate is the right register, not consecrate.
